questions.prompt: With zero resultant force, an object’s velocity is…
questions.explanation: Newton’s first law includes rest and uniform straight-line motion.

questions.prompt: Newton’s second law for constant mass is…
questions.explanation: Use the resultant force on the chosen body.

questions.prompt: Newton’s third-law pair acts on…
options: One body at two different times only
questions.explanation: Equal and opposite interaction forces act on the two interacting bodies.

questions.prompt: Why do third-law forces not cancel in one object’s free-body diagram?
options: The partner force acts on a different body
questions.explanation: Include only forces acting on the selected object.

questions.prompt: A trolley moving right can have zero resultant force when…
options: It moves right at constant velocity
questions.explanation: A nonzero velocity needs no resultant force to maintain it in the ideal model.

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force of 6 N acts on a 2 kg trolley. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = F_resultant/m = 6/2. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force of 10 N acts on a 5 kg trolley. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = F_resultant/m = 10/5. Result: 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force of 3 N acts on a 1.5 kg trolley. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = F_resultant/m = 3/1.5. Result: 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force of 12 N acts on a 4 kg trolley. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = F_resultant/m = 12/4. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: A constant resultant force of 8 N acts on a 2.5 kg trolley. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: a = F_resultant/m = 8/2.5. Result: 3.2 m/s².

questions.prompt: Resultant force is the…
options: Sum of all force magnitudes without direction
Vector sum of forces on one body
questions.explanation: Add forces with their directions.

questions.prompt: Two opposite horizontal forces of equal magnitude give…
options: Twice either force in one direction
questions.explanation: Equal opposite forces on the same body balance.

questions.prompt: With mass fixed, doubling nonzero resultant force doubles…
questions.explanation: a = F/m, so acceleration is proportional to resultant force.

questions.prompt: A body’s acceleration points in the direction of…
questions.explanation: Newton’s second law is a vector relation.

questions.prompt: Can a body slow down while accelerating right?
options: No, rightward acceleration always raises speed
Yes, if it is moving left
questions.explanation: Speed decreases when acceleration opposes velocity.

questions.prompt: Right is positive. A 2 kg body has a 10 N rightward force and a 4 N leftward force. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: F_net = 10 − 4; a = F_net/2. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: Right is positive. A 3 kg body has a 12 N rightward force and a 3 N leftward force. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: F_net = 12 − 3; a = F_net/3. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: Right is positive. A 1 kg body has a 8 N rightward force and a 6 N leftward force. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: F_net = 8 − 6; a = F_net/1. Result: 2 m/s².

questions.prompt: Right is positive. A 5 kg body has a 20 N rightward force and a 5 N leftward force. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: F_net = 20 − 5; a = F_net/5. Result: 3 m/s².

questions.prompt: Right is positive. A 2 kg body has a 5 N rightward force and a 9 N leftward force. Find acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: F_net = 5 − 9; a = F_net/2. Result: -2 m/s².

questions.prompt: Weight is measured in…
questions.explanation: Weight is gravitational force W = mg; mass is in kilograms.

questions.prompt: The normal contact force is directed…
options: Always vertically upwards on any slope
questions.explanation: Normal means perpendicular to the contact surface.

questions.prompt: On a horizontal surface with no vertical acceleration or other vertical forces, N equals…
questions.explanation: Vertical force balance gives N − mg = 0.

questions.prompt: On an incline with no other perpendicular forces, N is…
questions.explanation: Resolve weight perpendicular to the plane.

questions.prompt: The Moon has a smaller g than Earth. The same object has…
options: The same mass but less weight
questions.explanation: Mass is intrinsic in this model; weight depends on local g.

questions.prompt: What is the weight of a 1 kg mass near Earth? Use g = 9.81 m/s². Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: W = mg = 1 × 9.81. Result: 9.81 N.

questions.prompt: What is the weight of a 2 kg mass near Earth? Use g = 9.81 m/s². Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: W = mg = 2 × 9.81. Result: 19.6 N.

questions.prompt: What is the weight of a 3.5 kg mass near Earth? Use g = 9.81 m/s². Give the closest value.
What is the weight of a 5 kg mass near Earth? Use g = 9.81 m/s². Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: W = mg = 5 × 9.81. Result: 49.1 N.

questions.prompt: What is the weight of a 8 kg mass near Earth? Use g = 9.81 m/s². Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: W = mg = 8 × 9.81. Result: 78.5 N.

questions.prompt: Static friction can act on a block that…
options: Is at rest relative to the surface
questions.explanation: Static friction prevents relative sliding when within its limit.

questions.prompt: The maximum static-friction magnitude is modelled by…
questions.explanation: Actual static friction can be smaller than its limiting value.

questions.prompt: A 4 N pull is below the static-friction limit. The block remains still. Friction magnitude is…
questions.explanation: Static friction balances the applied force up to its limit.

questions.prompt: Sliding friction generally acts…
questions.explanation: Its direction resists relative sliding at the contact.

questions.prompt: Why does the simulator state that one μ is used for static and kinetic friction?
options: Friction is always independent of normal force
Real surfaces may have different μs and μk
questions.explanation: Using one coefficient is a simplifying assumption, not a universal material property.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg block starts at rest on a horizontal track. Pull = 4 N, μs = μk = 0.3, g = 9.81. Find acceleration after applying the pull. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: First compare the pull with μN. Static friction balances it below the limit; otherwise use F_net = pull − μmg, then a = F_net/m. Result: 0 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 2 kg block starts at rest on a horizontal track. Pull = 10 N, μs = μk = 0.2, g = 9.81. Find acceleration after applying the pull. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: First compare the pull with μN. Static friction balances it below the limit; otherwise use F_net = pull − μmg, then a = F_net/m. Result: 3.04 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 3 kg block starts at rest on a horizontal track. Pull = 12 N, μs = μk = 0.1, g = 9.81. Find acceleration after applying the pull. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: First compare the pull with μN. Static friction balances it below the limit; otherwise use F_net = pull − μmg, then a = F_net/m. Result: 3.02 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 1 kg block starts at rest on a horizontal track. Pull = 2 N, μs = μk = 0.4, g = 9.81. Find acceleration after applying the pull. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: First compare the pull with μN. Static friction balances it below the limit; otherwise use F_net = pull − μmg, then a = F_net/m. Result: 0 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 4 kg block starts at rest on a horizontal track. Pull = 15 N, μs = μk = 0.25, g = 9.81. Find acceleration after applying the pull. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: First compare the pull with μN. Static friction balances it below the limit; otherwise use F_net = pull − μmg, then a = F_net/m. Result: 1.3 m/s².

questions.prompt: The component of weight down an incline at angle θ is…
questions.explanation: Resolve the gravitational force parallel to the slope.

questions.prompt: A block can stay at rest on a rough incline when…
options: Static friction can balance mg sinθ
questions.explanation: Compare mg sinθ with μs mg cosθ.

questions.prompt: Increasing the angle of a frictionless incline makes down-slope acceleration…
questions.explanation: a = g sinθ rises over that angle interval.

questions.prompt: In the ideal sliding model with fixed angle and μ, changing mass changes acceleration by…
questions.explanation: Mass cancels from g(sinθ − μ cosθ).

questions.prompt: Why must the static limit be checked before applying a sliding-friction equation?
options: The block may remain at rest with adjusting friction
Static friction always equals μN exactly
The normal force is always zero
questions.explanation: A negative predicted downhill acceleration from the naive sliding formula need not imply uphill motion from rest.

questions.prompt: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 10°. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find down-slope acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: With no friction, a = g sinθ; use degree mode. Result: 1.7 m/s².

questions.prompt: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 20°. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find down-slope acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: With no friction, a = g sinθ; use degree mode. Result: 3.36 m/s².

questions.prompt: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 30°. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find down-slope acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: With no friction, a = g sinθ; use degree mode. Result: 4.9 m/s².

questions.prompt: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 40°. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find down-slope acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: With no friction, a = g sinθ; use degree mode. Result: 6.31 m/s².

questions.prompt: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 50°. Use g = 9.81 m/s². Find down-slope acceleration. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: With no friction, a = g sinθ; use degree mode. Result: 7.51 m/s².

questions.prompt: For a light inextensible string over an ideal pulley, connected bodies have…
options: Equal acceleration magnitudes along the string
questions.explanation: The string constraint ties their motions together while taut.

questions.prompt: An ideal massless, frictionless pulley gives string tension that is…
options: Equal on both sides of a light string
questions.explanation: The ideal string and pulley transmit a common tension.

questions.prompt: A hanging mass accelerating down has tension…
options: Equal to its weight in every case
questions.explanation: mg − T = ma; for a > 0, T < mg.

questions.prompt: When analysing the whole trolley-plus-hanging-mass system, tensions…
options: Must both be added as external driving forces
Become zero on each separate body
questions.explanation: Internal interactions cancel from the combined-system force balance, but remain in individual diagrams.

questions.prompt: If trolley static friction can balance the hanging weight, an initially resting system…
questions.explanation: Compare the hanging driving force with the available static-friction limit.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg trolley on a frictionless table is connected to a 1 kg hanging mass by a light string and ideal pulley. Use g = 9.81. Find their acceleration magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For the combined system, external driving force is m₂g and total mass is m₁ + m₂. Thus a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂). Result: 2.45 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 2 kg trolley on a frictionless table is connected to a 1 kg hanging mass by a light string and ideal pulley. Use g = 9.81. Find their acceleration magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For the combined system, external driving force is m₂g and total mass is m₁ + m₂. Thus a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂). Result: 3.27 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 4 kg trolley on a frictionless table is connected to a 2 kg hanging mass by a light string and ideal pulley. Use g = 9.81. Find their acceleration magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For the combined system, external driving force is m₂g and total mass is m₁ + m₂. Thus a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂). Result: 3.27 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 5 kg trolley on a frictionless table is connected to a 0.5 kg hanging mass by a light string and ideal pulley. Use g = 9.81. Find their acceleration magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For the combined system, external driving force is m₂g and total mass is m₁ + m₂. Thus a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂). Result: 0.892 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 1 kg trolley on a frictionless table is connected to a 2 kg hanging mass by a light string and ideal pulley. Use g = 9.81. Find their acceleration magnitude. Give the closest value.
questions.explanation: For the combined system, external driving force is m₂g and total mass is m₁ + m₂. Thus a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂). Result: 6.54 m/s².
